thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: realtime p99 latency spike detected for /v1/generate (hosted-us-east). p99 jumped from 280ms -> 2.4s in last 2m. paging oncall now :rotating_light:
maria.h: oncall ack. I see correlated increase in streaming stalls in the websocket tier, and a KCACHE miss rate spike.
sachin: looking at the dashboards now — top-level: per-region p99, backend service latencies, and kvcache hit-rate. Quick checks: is there a recent deploy?
jules: no deploy in last hour from deploy-bot. I pulled recent traces: a bunch of tail requests are showing long time in "streaming_write" phase, not model compute.
kevin: copying relevant logs to thread. snippet from ingress logs: ```
[ingress] 2025-11-04T18:02:14Z host=redwood-api-1 req_id=abc123 stage=ws_write duration=1800ms bytes=0 
[kvcache] miss_rate=0.67 rehydration=burst
```
nora: that kvcache miss_rate is nasty. Could be cache eviction storm after a hot restart. Are any nodes OOMing or restarting?
maria.h: kubectl get pods -n inference shows a couple of ws-proxy pods Cycling (CrashLoopBackoff) on us-east-1a. Getting pod logs now.
sachin: I can run a quick pod-level mitigation: scale up ws-proxy replicas to absorb backlog and route some traffic to us-west. Anyone object?
jules: +1, do it. Also enable streaming fallback to chunked-polling for sessions that are stuck. That should reduce time spent in ws_write.
ops_bot: executed: `kubectl scale deployment/ws-proxy --replicas=8 -n inference` by sachin — started at 18:05Z. :white_check_mark:
kevin: added temporary routing rule: route 25% of us-east traffic to us-west via smart-routing. Command: ```rbctl route set --service api --percent 25 --from us-east --to us-west```
nora: verifying metrics after scale/reroute... p95 improved to 420ms, p99 down to 1.1s (from 2.4s). kvcache missrate still high at 0.52 but trending down.
maria.h: can we identify which keys are thrashing the kvcache? Any recent request patterns?
sachin: sampling slow requests shows a common pattern: huge prompts from an internal batch job (analytics ingest) hitting the hosted API with long-context streaming. That explains kvcache churn. I found an internal job spike at 17:58Z.
jules: timeline: job spike -> ws-proxy pod restarts -> kvcache eviction storm -> streaming stalls -> p99 spike. Mitigation working. Next steps: throttle the analytics job and add kvcache warmup for large-context requests.
kevin: I've raised a temporary quota for the analytics token and added a circuit-breaker rule for streaming sessions that exceed N concurrent streams. Applied at 18:12Z.
nora: customer impact: looking at error budgets and billing logs — small fraction of requests saw >1s latency, mostly non-SL tier internal traffic, but some paid requests affected (~0.6% of traffic). I will file a customer-impact note to #support.
maria.h: support note draft: "We observed a brief p99 latency spike due to an internal bulk job causing cache eviction; mitigation applied (scale + reroute). Some customers experienced degraded streaming performance for ~15min. Investigating next steps." lmk edits.
sachin: ops postmortem checklist: collect traces, pod events, kvcache metric history, and the analytics job schedule. Also add an alert runbook update: when kvcache missrate >0.5 and ws_write duration >500ms, auto-scale ws-proxy and rate-limit bulk tokens.
jules: also consider adding a low-latency path: prefer cached prefixes and reject extremely long streaming sessions with a 429 for non-critical tokens.
kevin: rolling a canary config change to pre-warm kvcache on deploys to avoid this on restarts. Planning rollout to dedicated next week.
ops_bot: incident-bot follow-up: created incident report: INC-1758809999, severity: S1 (service degraded), timeline recorded.
nora: closing notes: p99 returned near baseline at 18:20Z after scaling and throttle. Monitoring for 45m. If metrics stay stable, we'll de-escalate and draft a short postmortem.
maria.h: thanks everyone. tagging @oncall for awareness and @support to send customer comms once we confirm duration. :thumbsup:
